title: Recover a hijacked domain or social account
summary: The first hour decides how far this spreads. Work out what was taken: the registrar account, DNS, email, or the social handle. Changed MX and DNS records are how one stolen login becomes all of them. Lock what you still hold: passwords, hardware-key 2FA, the registrar transfer lock. Then use the owners' own processes: the registrar's compromise case (if the domain was transferred away, ICANN's transfer-dispute path, where the 60-day rules matter) and the platforms' recovery flows (Google's hacked-account flow; Instagram's /hacked; X's sits behind its help center). Check registration state on RDAP instead of guessing. If posts went out or mail was read, tell the people affected before the screenshots do. A domain transferred to another registrar comes back only with pain.
